rationale.conceptual: The method is an established tight‑binding recursion technique (cluster Bethe Lattice) that needs careful implementation of the Green’s function procedure and handling of several defect configurations. It is not a standard library call, but the algorithm is documented in the paper and prior works (RP, LJC).
rationale.execution: Three logical steps (reference DOS for two hosts, then eight defect LDOS calculations) are all performed in one Python script using only numpy/scipy. No external data fetching, no multi‑tool orchestration, and straightforward I/O.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires implementing a tight-binding cluster Bethe Lattice recursion method to compute defect state energies in Si₃N₄ and SiO₂. The algorithm is non-trivial but well‑established and all parameters are given in the paper. The pipeline is simple: a single script can perform all calculations and output a JSON. Resource needs are negligible (CPU only, no data).

compute_estimate.reasoning: The tight‑binding recursion uses tiny matrices; all parameters are hardcoded from the paper’s tables. No large datasets are involved, and the computation is negligible (CPU only).
